sourceChecks.locator: National Institute of the Korean Language, ch. 12, PDF pp. 90–93 / lines 809–833: distinguishes subject honorification -시- from listener-directed endings -습니다/-요; levels vary by age, position, relationship and formality. Ch. 13, pp. 95–99 / lines 842–875: forms of address and names/titles.
sourceChecks.finding: Direct government support for the distinction between subject honorification and listener speech level, plus contextual variation; it does not establish Spanish usted equivalence or Spanish-specific judgments.

sourceChecks.locator: NIKL online Q&A, posted 24 June 2025, lines 172–190: listener honorification is identified from inflected forms, not the verb base form; lists speech levels.
sourceChecks.finding: Supports that speech-level classification is realized in inflected forms/endings, not a pronoun or citation form; no full translation guide.
